questions.text: What is software and software engineering? Explain the nature and characteristics of software. Justify the statement "Software does not wear out". Differentiate between software engineering and other engineering disciplines.

What is software crisis? Discuss the major factors and historical challenges responsible for software crisis in late 1960s, and explain how modern software engineering principles and practices help overcome it.
What are software myths? Discuss management myths, customer myths, and practitioner myths with suitable real-world examples and clarify the corresponding realities.
What is legacy software? Why is it challenging to maintain and evolve legacy software systems? Discuss strategies for legacy software re-engineering, reverse engineering, and modernization.
Explain software engineering code of ethics and professional practices (ACM/IEEE-CS Code of Ethics). Describe the eight principles governing ethical software development.
Differentiate between Generic Software Products and Custom (Bespoke) Software Products. Describe the major application categories of software (System, Embedded, Web, AI, Engineering/Scientific).
What is a Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC)? Explain generic framework activities (Communication, Planning, Modeling, Construction, Deployment) and Umbrella activities in software process.

Explain the Classical Waterfall Model and Modified Waterfall Model with block diagram. Discuss its advantages, limitations, and justify why it is unsuitable for projects requiring fast incremental releases.

Explain Evolutionary Process Models: Prototyping Model (Throwaway vs Evolutionary prototyping) and Boehm's Spiral Model. Detail the four quadrant activities in the Spiral model (Objective Setting, Risk Assessment, Development & Validation, Planning Next Phase) and explain why it suits high-risk projects.
Explain the Incremental Model and Rapid Application Development (RAD) model. Discuss their advantages, disadvantages, and suitability for real-world commercial software development.
What is Agile Software Development? Explain the 4 core values and 12 principles of the Agile Manifesto. Differentiate between Agile methodology and Plan-Driven (Traditional) process models.

Explain the Scrum Framework: Scrum Roles (Product Owner, Scrum Master, Development Team), Artifacts (Product Backlog, Sprint Backlog, Burndown / Burnup Charts), and Ceremonies (Sprint Planning, Daily Standup, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective).

Explain the Rational Unified Process (RUP). Describe the four phases of RUP (Inception, Elaboration, Construction, Transition) and core engineering workflows (Business Modeling, Requirements, Analysis & Design, Implementation, Test, Deployment).
Explain Extreme Programming (XP). Describe core XP practices: Pair Programming, Test-Driven Development (TDD), Refactoring, Collective Code Ownership, Simple Design, and Continuous Integration.

Explain the Software Requirements Engineering Process: Inception, Elicitation (Interviews, Questionnaires, JAD, Prototyping), Elaboration, Negotiation, Specification, and Validation. Justify why requirement discovery is difficult.

What is Software Requirements Specification (SRS)? What are the characteristics of a good SRS document (Unambiguous, Complete, Consistent, Verifiable, Modifiable, Traceable)? Describe the structure of an SRS document according to the IEEE 830 standard.

Differentiate between Functional and Non-Functional Requirements. Give examples of non-functional requirement categories (Performance, Reliability, Security, Usability, Portability) for an Online Banking or Airline Ticketing System.
Explain Agile Requirements Engineering: User Stories, Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then format), Story Points, Planning Poker, and Product Backlog grooming.
Differentiate between User Requirements and System Requirements. How are requirements validated using formal requirements reviews, prototyping, and test-case generation?
Explain Requirements Management and Traceability. Describe Forward Traceability, Backward Traceability, and how a Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM) is constructed and maintained.

Why is Software Architecture important? Explain the taxonomy of Architectural Styles: Layered Architecture, Client-Server (2-tier, 3-tier, Thin vs Fat client), Model-View-Controller (MVC), Pipe-and-Filter, and Microservices Architecture with diagrams.

Explain modular design principles. Define and differentiate between Cohesion and Coupling. Explain different types of Cohesion (Functional, Sequential, Communicational, Procedural, Temporal, Logical, Coincidental) and Coupling (Data, Stamp, Control, Common, Content). Why is High Cohesion and Low Coupling desired?

Explain Real-Time Software Systems. Differentiate between Hard Real-Time and Soft Real-Time systems. Describe the role and architecture of Real-Time Operating Systems (RTOS) and Data Acquisition Systems (DAS).

Explain Design Patterns in software design. Describe Creational (Singleton, Factory Method), Structural (Adapter, Composite), and Behavioral (Observer, Strategy) design patterns with diagrams and use-case examples.

Explain the concept of Software Architecture Evaluation. Describe the Architecture Tradeoff Analysis Method (ATAM) and how it evaluates quality attribute tradeoffs (Performance, Security, Modifiability).
Differentiate between Monolithic Architecture and Microservices Architecture. Explain API Gateways, service discovery, inter-service communication (REST vs gRPC), and database-per-service pattern.

What is a Data Flow Diagram (DFD)? Explain DFD symbols (Process, Data Flow, Data Store, External Entity) and DFD balancing rules. Draw Context Level (Level 0) and Level 1 DFD for an Online Food Ordering System or Airline Ticketing System.

Case Study: Suppose your team is developing an Airline Reservation System. Draw Context Level (Level 0) and Level 1 DFD showing customer account creation, flight search, ticket booking, payment gateway integration, and e-ticket generation.

What is Use Case Modeling in UML? Draw a comprehensive Use Case Diagram for an Automated Bus Ticket Issuing System or E-Commerce System showing Actors, Use Cases, `<<include>>`, `<<extend>>`, and generalization relationships.

Construct a Class Diagram for a Hospital Management System, ATM System, or Hotel Reservation System showing classes, attributes, methods, visibility indicators ($+,-,\#$), associations, multiplicity ($1..*$), aggregation, and composition.

Construct an Activity Diagram and Sequence Diagram for an Online Food Delivery or Car Rental System showing lifelines, synchronous messages, asynchronous messages, activation bars, swimlanes, decision diamonds, and fork/join synchronization bars.

Case Study: A Ride-Sharing platform (like Pathao/Uber) allows riders to request rides, drivers to accept/reject rides, tracks GPS locations, calculates fares, and processes digital payments. Draw: (a) Use Case Diagram, (b) Sequence Diagram for the ride booking flow.

Explain State Machine (Statechart) Diagrams in UML. Construct a state machine diagram for an Order Processing Lifecycle (Created, Pending Payment, Paid, Processing, Shipped, Delivered, Cancelled) showing states, transitions, events, and guard conditions.
Explain CRC (Class-Responsibility-Collaborator) modeling in Object-Oriented Analysis and Design. How does CRC modeling assist in identifying classes, methods, and collaborations?

Differentiate between Verification and Validation (V&V) in software engineering. Explain the V-Model of software development and testing, highlighting how verification and validation activities map to corresponding lifecycle phases.

Explain Black-Box (Functional) Testing techniques: Equivalence Class Partitioning (ECP) and Boundary Value Analysis (BVA). Design comprehensive test cases for a student marks input field accepting integer values between 0 and 100.

Explain White-Box (Structural) Testing: Statement Coverage, Branch/Decision Coverage, and Condition Coverage. Draw Control Flow Graph (CFG) and calculate Cyclomatic Complexity $V(G) = E - N + 2P$ or $V(G) = P + 1$ for a given code segment to determine the number of independent execution paths.

Explain Software Testing Levels: Unit Testing, Integration Testing (Top-Down integration with stubs, Bottom-Up integration with drivers, Big-Bang), System Testing, and Acceptance Testing (Alpha Testing vs Beta Testing).

Explain Software Cost Estimation models: Lines of Code (LOC) and Function Point Analysis (FPA). Explain Basic and Intermediate COCOMO (Constructive Cost Model) for Organic, Semidetached, and Embedded modes. Calculate effort $E = a (KLOC)^b$ and development time $D = c (E)^d$ for an organic software project of 48 KLOC.

A web-enabled software system is estimated to be 60 KLOC. Assuming the project is in semidetached mode with coefficients $a = 3.0, b = 1.12, c = 2.5, d = 0.35$, calculate: (a) Total effort in Person-Months, (b) Development time in calendar months, (c) Average staff size, and (d) Productivity rate.

Explain Function Point Analysis (FPA). An application has 10 low External Inputs (weight 3), 5 high External Outputs (weight 7), 13 average External Inquiries (weight 4), 7 average Internal Logical Files (weight 10), and 5 low External Interface Files (weight 5). If Complexity Adjustment Factor (CAF) is $1.10$, compute Unadjusted Function Points (UFP) and Adjusted Function Points (AFP).

Explain Halstead's Software Science metrics. Define vocabulary $n = n_1 + n_2$, length $N = N_1 + N_2$, volume $V = N \log_2 n$, difficulty $D = \frac{n_1}{2} \frac{N_2}{n_2}$, and effort $E = D \times V$ with a given code example.

Explain Formal Technical Reviews (FTR) and Software Inspection process. What are the key objectives, participants roles (Moderator, Author, Reviewer, Scribe), and types of faults uncovered through formal inspections?

Define Software Quality Assurance (SQA). Differentiate between SQA and Quality Control (Testing). Explain McCall's Quality Factors organized under Product Operation, Product Revision, and Product Transition.

Explain SEI Capability Maturity Model Integration (CMMI). Describe the 5 Maturity Levels (Initial, Managed, Defined, Quantitatively Managed, Optimizing). How does CMMI differ from ISO 9001 quality standards?

Explain Software Reliability and Software Availability. Define Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF), Mean Time To Failure (MTTF), and Mean Time To Repair (MTTR). Explain software safety and hazard analysis.
Explain Software Maintenance and its four types: Corrective, Adaptive, Perfective, and Preventive maintenance with examples. Why is software maintenance the most cost-intensive phase in SDLC?

Explain Component-Based Software Engineering (CBSE). Describe the process for CBSE *with reuse* and CBSE *for reuse* with block diagrams. Discuss the benefits, challenges, and Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) component integration.

Explain Statistical Software Quality Assurance (Statistical SQA) and the Pareto Principle (80/20 rule - the "vital few" causes). How does Error Tracking and Defect Removal Efficiency (DRE) measure SQA effectiveness?
Explain Software Cleanroom Engineering approach. How does Cleanroom engineering integrate formal mathematical specification, statistical quality verification, and zero-defect code development?

What is Software Configuration Management (SCM)? Explain SCM elements: Configuration Identification, Version Control, Change Control (Change Control Board - CCB process), Configuration Audit, and Status Reporting. Differentiate between Version, Variant, and Release.

Explain modern Version Control Systems (Git), Git branching strategies (Git-flow: main, develop, feature, release, hotfix branches), and how pull requests / code reviews enforce software configuration baselines.
Explain Software Configuration Audit: Functional Configuration Audit (FCA) vs Physical Configuration Audit (PCA). Describe how baseline integrity is verified.

Explain the Change Control Process in detail. Draw a flowchart illustrating how a Change Request (CR) is submitted, evaluated by the CCB, approved/rejected, implemented, audited, and released as a new baseline.

Explain DevOps culture and Continuous Integration / Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipelines. Describe how automated testing, containerization (Docker), and orchestration (Kubernetes) enable rapid and reliable software releases.

Write technical notes on modern trends in software engineering: (a) AI-Assisted Software Development and LLM code synthesis, (b) Microservices vs Monolithic Architecture, (c) Serverless Computing, and (d) Green/Sustainable Software Engineering.
Explain Cloud-Native Architecture and Infrastructure as Code (IaC). Describe how tools like Terraform and Ansible automate cloud resource provisioning and configuration.
Explain Site Reliability Engineering (SRE). Define Service Level Objectives (SLO), Service Level Agreements (SLA), Service Level Indicators (SLI), and Error Budgets in modern software operations.
